key_insight: A quantum one-class model with only 2 qubits outperformed classical baselines for early impersonation-fraud detection after digital account opening, especially under extreme class imbalance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests QML may be practically useful for risk scoring in digital banking when fraud is rare, operational costs of false positives matter, and hardware-validated deployment is desired.
method: Compared quantum one-class classification using Automatic Quantum Feature Mapping (AQFM) against classical one-class methods.
Trained and evaluated on a real 2025 BCI cohort of 3,419 account openings with 8 confirmed fraud cases.
Validated the best 2-qubit setup on SpinQ Triangulum II NMR hardware and tested threshold transfer to an independent 2026 cohort.
evidence_signal: On the 2025 cohort, AQFM detected 7 of 8 frauds (88% recall) with 9.21% precision and about 70% fewer false positives than the best classical baseline at similar recall; on the 2026 cohort it detected 20 of 31 frauds (64.5% recall) with 8.81% precision.
watch_item: Precision remains low because the positive class is extremely rare, so operational deployment still requires careful thresholding, drift monitoring, and cost-sensitive review design.
paper_title: Quantum Machine Learning for Few-Shot Impersonation Detection in Digital Account Opening
